newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market standstill -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market standstill -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade was at a standstill early Friday, with no reported bids or trades following this week's active sales, which depleted most showlists and kept feedlots current, cattle feeders said.
The bulk of this week's cattle sold on Wednesday at $65.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from light sales Tuesday and late last week, but steady with tops early last week.

"There won't be anything happening today," one Texas Panhandle feedlot manager said, "this will be a day to get caught up on the paperwork and see what happens with the cattle on feed report this afternoon," he said.

Friday's monthly USDA Cattle on Feed Report was expected to show on-feed numbers as of Aug 1 at 115.6 percent of year-ago levels, according to the average of analysts' pre-report estimates. July placements were seen at an average of 100.8 percent and July marketings at 105.5 percent.

Unless the report shows a hefty increase in placements, which could pressure CME live cattle futures, fed cattle prices next week were seen steady to higher amid outlooks for a decline in showlists, several feedlot sources said.
Projections for firm beef prices next week also could lend support to fed cattle prices, they said.
